surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the interaction between diethyl zinc (DEZ) and pentakis-dimethylamino tantalum (PDMAT) on a hydroxylated surface. The PDMAT pulse leads to the formation of ethane (m/e = 27) due to ligand exchange reactions, which subsequently decays as the surface reactions reach equilibrium. The presence of Ta5+ affects the surface reactions by altering the oxygen vacancy dynamics and influencing the growth of ZnO layers.
evidence: The surface reactions are studied using in situ downstream quadrupole mass spectrometry. The text describes the interaction between DEZ and PDMAT on a hydroxylated surface, with the formation of ethane (m/e = 27) during the ALD process. The presence of Ta5+ is shown to affect the surface reactions by altering the oxygen vacancy dynamics and influencing the growth of ZnO layers. The text also discusses the formation of TaZn and the role of oxygen vacancies and zinc vacancies in the doping mechanism.
